result.title: Hidden Data Challenges in Clinical Machine Learning
result.summary: Widely reused preprocessing pipelines for electronic health records can encode assumptions about when information became available, what clinical episode a label represents, and what missingness means. These assumptions are rarely audited systematically and may propagate across subsequent studies when preprocessing pipelines are reused or adapted. Using MIMIC-IV as a case study, we identify and quantify violations of three complementary forms of preprocessing alignment, i.e., temporal, semantic, and population alignment, which manifest as temporal leakage, feature-task misalignment, and biased imputation. We show how ambiguities in timestamp semantics, episode definitions, endpoint construction, modality selection, and missingness handling can alter the information available to a model and affect the interpretation of its predictions. Through analyses of MIMIC-IV data and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that such choices may remain largely invisible in aggregate predictive performance while changing the signals on which models rely. We derive practical recommendations for temporally valid, clinically aligned, and reproducible preprocessing of MIMIC-IV and related electronic health record datasets. The code for our experiments, including our proposed preprocessing, is available at: https://github.com/m2l-lab/mimic-iv-preprocess.

AI.brief_summary: 以 MIMIC-IV 为案例，审计 EHR 预处理中时序、语义与人群对齐三类违规（时序泄漏、特征-任务错配、有偏插补），量化其如何改变模型可获得的信息与预测解释，并给出可复现的预处理建议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息何时可用、缺失与插补意味着什么」的审计视角，可能可供核查 VLM/LVR 推理评测中证据可用性与隐性信息泄漏（聚合指标掩盖信号变化）的问题，属远领域概念线索，需较多迁移核查。
